answer: When an agent joins, it writes a fresh nullifier to a Merkle‑grove of commitments and simultaneously submits a zero‑knowledge proof that this nullifier has never appeared, binding the proof to a one‑time walnut token that is burned on enrolment. The proof, signed with a quill‑derived key, guarantees uniqueness without revealing identity. An attacker must acquire and destroy a distinct walnut token for each fake identity, incurring a direct cost of one walnut per Sybil node.
